name: Setting up the light behind the TV

pages.name: Telling the hub where the screen is and which way the strip runs

artboards.title: Today: the light behind the TV has no way to be set up
A, then: which way the strip runs
B: mark the screen on a phone

annotations.text:
WHY THIS EXISTS

Step 5 of the living room, the camera way (20 November 2026): a camera across the room reads the TV's picture and the strip behind the TV follows its edges. The strip and the hub can do that now (strip/firmware follow mode, startup/glow.py). Two things only the household can tell it: where the TV is in the camera's view, and which way the strip runs around the TV.

A: THE TV FINDS ITSELF. The hub draws the TV, so it can put four white corners on it and find them in the camera's view itself; nobody marks anything. Then the strip lights a moving light from its start and the TV asks, with the remote, which corner it started from and which way it went. FOR: done from the sofa in under a minute, and redone the same way after the camera is moved. AGAINST: a bright room or a camera that sees only part of the screen needs B as the way out.

B: MARK IT ON A PHONE

The camera's picture on a phone, with four dots to drag to the TV's corners. FOR: works whatever the room, and the household sees exactly what the camera sees. AGAINST: fiddly on a small screen, and it means the camera's picture is shown on a phone, which a household should be asked about first.

PICK ONE

A, B, A with B when the TV can't find itself, or something else -- describe it. The strip's own card then gets a Follows the TV switch.
